In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal No(S). Of 2026
 (@ Slp(Crl.) No(S).

16644/2025)
 FIROZ @ FIZZU Appellant(s  VERSUS  THE STATE OF UTTAR PRADESH
Respondent  O R D E R Leave granted.

This appeal challenges the order dated 16.05.2023 passed by the High Court of Judicature at Allahabad at Lucknow Bench, in I.A. No. 9 of 2023 in Criminal Appeal No.172/2016 whereby the appellants application for suspension of sentence was dismissed.
The appellant Firoz @ Fizzu faced trial in connection with crime registered pursuant to FIR 554/2010 dated 05.11.2010 registered at P.S. Majhila, District Hardoi in respect of the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 304B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 [in short IPC] and under Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

entities.text: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad at Lucknow Bench
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The Trial Court convicted the appellant for the offence under Section 302 of the IPC vide judgment dated 13.01.2016 and sentenced him to life imprisonment along with a fine of Rs. 20,000/- therefor, and also convicted him for the offence under Sections 3 and 25 of the Arms Act and sentenced him for rigorous imprisonment for a period of 2 years along with a fine of Rs.5000/- therefor.
The appellant, being aggrieved by the order of conviction passed by the Trial Court, filed Criminal Appeal No. 172/2016 before the High Court and the same is pending before the High Court.

During the pendency of the said Criminal Appeal, the appellant filed an application bearing C.M.
Application No. 14958/2016 before the High Court seeking suspension of sentence.

The High Court,
by the order dated 02.11.2016 rejected the application.

A second application bearing C.M.
Application No. 73801 of 2017 was then preferred by the appellant but the same, too, was rejected by the High Court vide order dated 02.09.2022.
Vide the impugned order dated 16.05.2023, the High Court also dismissed the third application filed by the appellant being I.A. No. 09/2023 for suspension of sentence.
Hence, the present criminal appeal.
This Court, vide its order dated 06.10.2025, issued notice in the instant matter.

Heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for the State and perused the material on record.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the appellant has completed fourteen years of actual incarceration and therefore the High Court was not right in dismissing I.A. No.9/2023 which was for seeking suspension of sentence and bail.
He further submitted that the appeal is of the year 2016 and having regard to the huge pendency before the Allahabad High Court inevitably there would be a delay in the hearing of this appeal.
He further submitted that the appellant has a good case on merits.

Bearing in mind these facts, he submitted that the impugned order may be set aside and the relief of suspension of sentence and bail be granted to the appellant herein pending disposal of the appeal before the High Court.

Per contra, learned standing counsel for the respondent-State with reference to his counter affidavit contended that the conviction of the appellant is under Section 302 of the IPC and he has been imposed the sentence of life imprisonment and fine and the allegations as against the appellant under the Arms Act have also been proved.
It was contented that there is no merit in this appeal.
Considering the facts on record, in our view, the case for suspension of sentence is made out.

We,
therefore, allow this appeal and direct as under:
The appellant shall be produced before the concerned Trial Court as early as possible and the Trial Court shall release him on bail, subject to such conditions as it may deem appropriate to impose to ensure his presence in the proceedings.
The appellant shall appear before the High Court as and when directed to do so.
It is directed that the appellant shall extend complete cooperation in the hearing of the appeal before the High Court.
The appellant shall not misuse his liberty in any manner.
Any infraction of the conditions shall entail cancellation of the suspension of sentence granted to the appellant.
With these observations, the Criminal Appeal is allowed.

J . ( B . V . N A G A R A T H N A )
J. ( UJJAL BHUYAN ) NEW DELHI;
